subject: Coordinating group demo: waitlist handling + host queue
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Claire Lin <claire@brightside.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Coordinating group demo: waitlist handling + host queue

Hi Claire, Tom —

Thanks again for your interest in Redwood. We have a couple of prospects who signed up for the same group demo slot next week; rather than run separate sessions we usually batch similar customers together and operate a short waitlist + host-queue for overflow. Before I lock anything down I wanted to run our suggested flow by you both and confirm timing constraints.

Proposal (brief):
- 45 minute group demo + 15 minute open Q&A.
- If more than 12 registrants show up, attendees beyond 12 join a waiting queue; we push them a short follow-up recording + offer a 1:1 if they need a dedicated walkthrough.
- We'll prioritize live Q&A for customers who raised security/compliance questions in pre-demo form.

Questions for you:
1) Do you want Brightside-specific content (security/pricing deep-dive) in the first 15 minutes or as a breakout after the main demo?
2) Any firm blackout windows (dates/times we should avoid)?
3) Are you comfortable with recording and sharing the condensed recording with waitlist attendees?

Attached: initial attendee matrix (blank) — fill it with named registrants and any known compliance/contract flags and send back.

If it helps, Neha (cc) can own the waitlist routing and Ben will run the bridge/host queue.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: attendee_matrix_v1.csv (CSV stub)

From: Claire Lin <claire@brightside.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@enterpriseco.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coordinating group demo: waitlist handling + host queue

Hi Irene —

This approach sounds good to us. A couple of notes:
- Brightside would prefer a 50/10 split (50-min demo, 10-min Q&A) if your schedule allows — we have a heavy integration question set.
- For content, please include a short section (5–7 minutes) on private deployment and data residency early in the demo — that's our execs' top priority.
- Recording is fine as long as the recording is gated to attendees + waitlist registrants only (no public posting).

I'll attach our current registrant list — two of our folks (Amanda H. and Raul S.) flagged SOC 2 questions specifically. I can drop their names in the attendee matrix after this thread.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Lin
Head of Partnerships
Brightside AI

Thanks Claire — I pulled an availability grid and pre-filled the matrix with the two Brightside names you mentioned.

Operational notes from my side:
- I'll own the waitlist: if >12 people join, I'll send an automated "you're on the waitlist" email with the recording promise and a Calendly link for 1:1 follow-up.
- If someone marks "security/compliance" as a priority, they get priority position in the host queue for Q&A (we surface that in the joining lobby).
- Fallback plan: if more than half of registrants drop out inside 24 hrs, we reschedule to a dedicated Brightside slot. See attached runbook.

Irene — you mentioned Ben will run the bridge. Ben, can you confirm you can host the live Q&A after the 50 minute demo? If not, we can flip the Q&A to earlier.
